subject: Procurement: tiered rebate structure and PO mandates
messages:
From: Sofia Turner <sofia.turner@mediflow.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Mediflow Procurement <procurement@mediflow.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tiered rebate structure + PO requirements

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to surface a few constraints before we get to legal:

- We need every invoice to carry our PO number (master PO + sub-POs are ok).
- Standard net terms are Net45 for our vendors; we can consider Net30 for strategic partners but requires AP approval.
- We prefer consolidated monthly invoices rather than weekly micro-invoices (our ERP can’t ingest high-frequency billing).
- For the rebate structure we discussed: procurement needs the conditional thresholds spelled out in the SOW (milestones or revenue triggers) and an example invoice/credit flow.

Can your team outline how Redwood would apply a tiered rebate if we hit $1M and $2.5M ARR thresholds, and what invoice cadence is required to make that work operationally? Also confirm whether Redwood can accept a single quarterly master PO or needs a PO per invoice.

Appreciate a concise MA (mutual action) / example invoice flow we can share with AP.

Thanks,
Sofia Turner
Sourcing Manager — Mediflow Health
Sofia.Turner@mediflow.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered rebate structure + PO requirements

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for laying that out — helpful. High level answers up front, details below:

1) PO on every invoice: we can include the PO number on each invoice. If you issue a single master PO with line-item references for the quarter that works; our billing needs either the PO on every invoice or a PO reference map in the SOW.

2) Net terms: Net45 is fine; Net30 can be made available as a billing option but typically affects rebate timing. We can model a rebate that posts as a credit on the invoice following the threshold trigger (so if you hit $1M in April, credit applied on May invoice).

3) Invoice cadence: monthly consolidated invoices are the simplest for ERP ingestion and do not materially impact our ability to track thresholds. Weekly invoices are supported but will complicate crediting and reconciliation on both sides.

4) Rebate structure: we can support a tiered % rebate (example: 3% at $1M, 5% at $2.5M) with lookback and grace period. We typically require a 30-day reconciliation window to validate usage-based triggers before issuing credits.

Cc’ing Vanessa (AM) to confirm operational flow and Priya (Billing/Finance) to confirm how credits would be represented on statements.

Next steps: I’ll attach a short MA plan and a toy rebate table for your review. Can you confirm whether AP will accept consolidated monthly invoices referencing the master PO and whether they require any specific invoice fields beyond PO#, invoice date, net terms, and tax/BU coding?

Best,
Marcus Lin

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered rebate structure + PO requirements

Hi Sofia —

Adding a couple operational clarifications from our side:

- Invoice format: we will include PO#, Redwood invoice number, invoice date, net terms, line-item usage (hours/tokens or bundled seat charge), tax ID, and a short memo line for your internal BU code. If you have a CSV schema, we can match it.
- Consolidation: monthly consolidated invoices are our recommended default for large enterprise customers — reduces disputes and simplifies credit application.
- Credit application: rebates will appear as negative line-items on subsequent invoice(s). For large credits (> $25k) we can issue a separate credit memo if your AP prefers that.
- Master PO approach: if you issue one master quarterly PO, please provide a PO mapping table (PO -> invoice period mapping) at contract kickoff; we’ll store that as an invoice reference.

Priya — can you confirm the timeline for issuing a credit memo vs applying an on-invoice credit? Also, does Redwood require any minimum invoice frequency to maintain rebate eligibility?

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Director — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Turner <sofia.turner@mediflow.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tiered rebate structure + PO requirements

Hi all —

Operational notes from Finance:

- Credit mechanics: our preference is to apply rebates as negative line items on the next monthly invoice following validation. If Mediflow needs a separate credit memo for internal reconciliation, we can issue one within 10 business days of the validated trigger.
- Validation window: we require a 30-day lookback to validate usage and rule out anomalies. That means a threshold breach in April would be reflected as a credit on the May invoice after reconciliation.
- Minimum invoice frequency: we do not require weekly invoices to keep rebate eligibility — monthly consolidated invoices are fine. We only require clear invoice-period mapping to avoid double-counting.
- PO acceptance: we can work with a master quarterly PO. However, each invoice must include a PO reference (the master PO + invoice period) so AR can match.

Sofia — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call to walk through a sample reconciliation spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Billing Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com

Thanks Marcus/Vanessa/Priya — this is helpful. A few clarifications from AP and procurement here: 

- Mediflow confirmed they will issue a single quarterly master PO but require the following on each invoice: PO#, PO line reference, invoice period (start/end), and a CSV upload that maps invoice lines to our internal GL codes.
- Net45 is acceptable; the business will consider Net30 as part of a negotiated prepay volume commitment but won’t commit until discounts are finalized.
- Rebate thresholds: procurement would like the 3% at $1M and 5% at $2.5M documented in the SOW, with example calculations for a sample quarter. They also asked for the sample CSV format your team will provide for reconciliation.

Next steps from Mediflow:
1) Please send the MA plan and the sample rebate table with an example invoice and the CSV schema we’d need to ingest into our ERP.
2) We will route to AP and legal for SOW language.

If you can get the two attachments over by EOD tomorrow we’ll start internal routing.

Best,
